text: Beatrix finds a vintage denim jacket priced at $18 at a thrift store. She makes small repairs and lists it with a 35% markup. What is her selling price?

steps.caption: convert the percent to a decimal so we can multiply
find the dollar amount of the markup
add the markup to the original price

selfExplanation.question: Why add the markup back to the original price?

options.label: the selling price is the cost plus the profit

text: Beatrix sold a leather bag for $30 that she bought for $20. What was her profit margin as a percent of her cost?

steps.caption: divide profit by COST (not selling price) to get the margin

selfExplanation.question: Why divide by the cost, not the selling price?

options.label: profit margin tells you the return on what you paid
the selling price is always bigger so it would give a smaller number

text: A pair of vintage boots is listed at $50. The store is running a 20% off sale. What is the sale price?

steps.caption: instead of finding the discount and subtracting, find what fraction remains
multiply to get the sale price directly

selfExplanation.question: Why is multiplying by 0.80 faster than calculating the discount and subtracting?

options.label: one operation instead of two — same result
it gives a more accurate answer
discounts can only be calculated this way

text: Beatrix buys a bundle of 5 vintage t-shirts for $40 total. What is the cost per t-shirt?

steps.caption: to find the price per unit, divide total cost by quantity

options.label: to split the total cost equally across the shirts
subtraction would give a negative number

text: Beatrix bought a coat for $15 and spent $5 on repairs. She wants to sell it with a 40% markup on her TOTAL cost. What is her selling price?

steps.caption: first find her total investment in the coat
multiply by 1 + the markup percent to add the profit in one step

selfExplanation.question: Why include the repair cost in the markup base?

options.label: she needs to recover ALL her costs before profit

text: Beatrix bought a $32 sweater. New York City sales tax is 8.875%. What does she pay at the register, rounded to the nearest cent?

steps.caption: convert the tax rate to a decimal
calculate the tax on the sweater (rounds to $2.84)
add the tax to the price

selfExplanation.question: Why does the answer need rounding?

options.label: money only goes to two decimal places (cents)
to make it easier to count
